title: Accept an Export Without Holding the Request
description: Account exports take 20 minutes. The caller needs proof that work was accepted and a way to check progress. Which API contract fits?

options.text: Return 200 before recording anything and hope a worker sees the request.
options.explanation: A crash can lose unrecorded work after the client was told it succeeded.

options.text: Durably record a job, return 202 with its ID, and expose status from a job table.
options.explanation: Acceptance is synchronous and durable; execution is asynchronous. Reliable enqueueing needs an outbox or a recovery sweeper.

options.text: Keep the HTTP request open for all 20 minutes.
options.explanation: Proxy timeouts, deploys and retries make long work on the request path fragile.

options.text: Use the queue itself as the client's queryable job-status database.
options.explanation: A delivery queue is not the authoritative status record queried by job ID.
